title: How to Avoid Rookie Plumbing Mistakes: Strap Wrenches, Old-Pipe Techniques, and Radiant Floor Caution
summary: This Old House host demonstrates common plumbing missteps and practical corrections. The video covers preventing chrome fixture damage by using a strap wrench instead of pliers, preserving the roundness of old pipes with a three-corner bite when loosening, and a cautionary anecdote about radiant-floor installations that emphasizes checking screw size to avoid protruding fasteners. The demonstrations translate into user-friendly tips homeowners can apply during DIY plumbing projects.

sections.title: Intro: Common rookie plumbing mistakes
sections.description: Host frames the video as a tour of common mistakes homeowners make on DIY plumbing projects.

sections.title: Using a strap wrench to protect chrome fixtures
sections.description: Demonstrates how a strap wrench avoids scratching chrome fixtures and enables removal of difficult shapes like a tub spout.

sections.title: Three-corner bite to back out old piping
sections.description: Explains why a conventional wrench can deform round piping and shows using a three-corner bite to keep the pipe round while loosening.

sections.title: Radiant-floor installation: plates and tubing context
sections.description: Related anecdote illustrating radiant-floor components and how installations are visually and practically integrated.

sections.title: Screw-size lesson: check screws before finishing
sections.description: Narrative emphasizes checking screw size and quantity to avoid protruding fasteners, using a radiant-floor example of mis-sizing screws.

sections.title: Wrap-up and closing tips
sections.description: Closing remarks and acknowledgments, summarizing practical takeaways from the segment.
